Package org.geysermc.paletter.internal.component

Class Transforms

java.lang.Object
org.geysermc.paletter.internal.component.Transforms
public final class Transforms extends Object
The hand transforms: the fields no rule inferred from the BDS captures explains. The code generator's table (HandTransforms in the tools) names the field each method encodes; the generated encoders call Transforms.name(ctx, node, owner) with the node the owner writes to and the record that holds the field (the component itself for a whole component transform), so a name the table gives and this class lacks does not compile. Overloads per owner type.

Each method's Javadoc says why no inferred rule explains its field and what evidence its output rests on. Where BDS builds differ, the method compares WireContext.protocol() with the generated ComponentIndex constant of the first capture that shows the newer shape.

  • Method Details

    • collisionBoxes

      public static void collisionBoxes(@NonNull WireContext ctx, @NonNull WireNode out, @NonNull CollisionBox c)
      minecraft:collision_box as a list of boxes: enabled and per box min/max in 0..16 block space; the boolean form is written by the generated rules. Each min/max leaf depends on both origin and size (and BDS orders min and max per axis), so fitting one field at a time gives conflicting linear rules on every leaf.

      y is origin.y to origin.y + size.y, z 8 + origin.z to that plus size.z. x runs like z in the captures of BDS 1.26.36.1 to 1.26.52.3; from 1.26.63.1 BDS mirrors it: minX = 8 - origin.x - size.x, maxX = 8 - origin.x.

    • geometry

      public static void geometry(@NonNull WireContext ctx, @NonNull WireNode out, @NonNull Geometry c)
      minecraft:geometry, in the shape every BDS 1.26.63.1 capture shows: the description fields plus four flags BDS always sends as 0 (ignoreGeometryForIsSolid, isV1Fullblock, needsLegacyTopRotation, useBlockTypeLightAbsorption), unset fields as BDS sends them (culling "", culling_layer undefined). Bone visibility is a Molang expression, kept as a string like BDS does; the constants true/false become "1.000000"/"0.000000", which no rule over the JSON value fits.

      BDS sends n_way_visual_rotation from 1.26.63.1 on, every axis, "" for an axis not set. The captures of BDS 1.26.36.1 to 1.26.52.3 rejected the base of the component, so their shape is this one without it.

    • materialInstances

      public static void materialInstances(@NonNull WireContext ctx, @NonNull WireNode out, @NonNull MaterialInstances c)
      minecraft:material_instances: face aliases to mappings, faces to materials, face dimming, isotropic and alpha_masked_tint packed into packed_bools (bits 0, 1 and 3; bit 2, SUPPORTS_TEXTURE_VARIATIONS_BIT, always set), defaults as BDS sends them. The flags share one byte, so each field's value table only fits with the others at their default, and the faces and aliases of one JSON object split into two compounds: the rules inferred per field describe neither.

    • blockDescriptorStates

      public static void blockDescriptorStates(@NonNull WireContext ctx, @NonNull WireNode out, BlockPlacer.UseOn d)
      The states of a block descriptor (block_placer.use_on, entity_placer.use_on and dispense_on, digger.destroy_speeds[].block, placement_filter block filters): a compound of state values, typed like the named block's states in the palette's registry (booleans as bytes; pillar_axis "y" becomes 0).     • blockName

      public static void blockName(@NonNull WireContext ctx, @NonNull WireNode out, @NonNull BlockPlacer c)
      block_placer.block: the block's name (a name without namespace gets minecraft:, as BDS 1.26.x sends "dirt"), or an empty string for a vanilla block this version does not have. BDS resolves the name against its block registry: the captures of 1.26.45.1 and 1.26.52.3 send minecraft:ice_crystal and minecraft:icicle as "", that of 1.26.63.1 as named, so the leaf depends on the version's blocks, not on the JSON value. A name of another namespace is a custom block, which may be registered after the item, so it is sent as it is.

      public static void ammunitionItemDescriptor(@NonNull WireContext ctx, @NonNull WireNode out, @NonNull Shooter.Ammunition c)
      ammunition[].item: an item descriptor: {name} for an item the registry knows, {} for any other descriptor (the captures send "item": {} and objects without a name as {}, where the inferred identity of item.name would leave the compound out); an entry without item is sent with the empty descriptor too.

    • itemDescriptorList

      public static void itemDescriptorList(@NonNull WireContext ctx, @NonNull WireNode out, @NonNull Repairable c)
      repair_items: items as [{name}] (names as written, not namespaced; or one {tags} Molang query), an entry without known items dropped with its repair amount. The repair amount is a float for a number and Molang for a string: the two JSON types land on the same leaf with different NBT types, which no single rule fits. BDS 1.26.36.1 sends the Molang as a compound {expression, version: 0s} (-1s for an empty expression), 1.26.45.1 and later as a string.
